issue_label: Remedy for Above-Ceiling Delay — Stay of Proceedings

default_authority.principle: Where net delay exceeds the presumptive ceiling and the Crown cannot rebut the presumption of unreasonable delay, a stay of proceedings is the remedy. The stay is the sole remedy for pre-verdict above-ceiling delay under current law.

jurisdiction_variants.variance_description: The ONCA in R v R.B.-C. (2024 ONCA 930) applied a sentence reduction rather than a stay for post-verdict sentencing delay (Charley framework). This is now at the SCC (File 41677). This variant applies only to post-verdict delay; pre-verdict above-ceiling delay remains stay-only in Ontario.

controlling_authority.principle: For post-verdict sentencing delay, a sentence reduction may be an appropriate remedy in lieu of a stay (Charley framework). Does not apply to pre-verdict above-ceiling delay.

jurisdiction_variants.notes: R.B.-C. is now at the SCC (File 41677). If SCC endorses sentence reduction for post-verdict delay, this creates a precedent for remedial flexibility that may pressure the pre-verdict stay-only rule.

pending_authority.issue: Whether the complexity exception scope should be expanded; AG BC argues Jordan framework is 'an anomaly' and urges 'greater remedial flexibility'
pending_authority.potential_impact: Decided 2026-05-29 (R v Vrbanic, 2026 SCC 19). The Court REFUSED to create a residual remedial discretion ('would resurrect the Morin balancing Jordan was meant to bury'); the stay REMAINS the automatic remedy for a proven pre-verdict breach. It did signal that Rahey may be revisited in a future case (para 81), so remedial flexibility remains a live forward question.
pending_authority.resolution_note: Decided as R v Vrbanic, 2026 SCC 19. Outcome REINFORCED the stay-only rule for now (residual discretion refused), with a forward signal (Rahey may be revisited). Pending Michael review.

pending_authority.issue: Whether sentence reduction is a valid remedy for post-verdict delay in lieu of a stay
pending_authority.potential_impact: Heard 2026-01-16; judgment reserved as of 2026-06-08. The case to watch for whether the SCC will endorse a non-stay remedy (the thread Vrbanic left open re Rahey). If affirmed, remedial-flexibility precedent that may pressure the pre-verdict stay-only rule.

pending_authority.issue: Would legislate that a stay should not be ordered unless the court is satisfied no other remedy would be appropriate
pending_authority.potential_impact: If proclaimed in force: courts would be required to consider alternatives to a stay before ordering one. Advanced to report stage (committee reported with amendments 2026-05-25; report-stage debate began 2026-06-03; time-allocation motion carried 2026-06-04). Still NOT law: no third reading, no Senate passage, no Royal Assent, no proclamation.

notes: Vrbanic (2026 SCC 19) RESOLVED and reinforced the pre-verdict stay-only rule today (residual discretion refused). Tier 4 retained because two forward pressures remain: R.B.-C. (SCC 41677, reserved) on a non-stay remedy for post-verdict delay, and the Court's own signal that Rahey may be revisited; plus Bill C-16 (report stage, not yet law). App remedy output should keep a third-category placeholder for possible future remedial flexibility. The Vrbanic amber banner can be retired; a Bill C-16 / R.B.-C. watch banner remains appropriate.
